A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same synthetic object-composition research, renamed from SOS to SOC. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including the galleries removed from v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection, segmentation, and grounding experiments, component and scaling ablations, FID measurements, and a human assessment of synthetic segments.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and reports additional synthetic-baseline comparisons and revised component ablations.

M1.justification: v1 uses uniformly sampled 2D positions and prescribed object-size bins. v2 replaces this with category-independent 3D position/depth sampling, category-dependent physical sizes, and perspective projection, then adds zoom/cropping and depth-of-field augmentation. It also introduces soft matting. IC-Light background generation and mask-area-weighted blending already existed in v1.

E1.justification: The represented tasks and benchmark coverage remain detection, segmentation, grounding, and intra-class referring on the same LVIS, COCO, OdinW-35, RefCOCO-family, gRefCOCO, DoD, and COCO/OpenImages-derived data. The synthetic category sources are retained. New comparator and component experiments do not establish additional task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Table 5 adds evaluated SegGen comparisons on COCO segmentation and LVIS-Mini detection, and SynGround on gRefCOCO; v1's corresponding quantitative table contains only Copy-Paste and X-Paste. v2 also adds LayoutGPT to the layout ablation and removes the Subject200K quantitative ablation row, although Appendix D.1 retains its comparison claim.

E3.justification: The revised ablation design explicitly disables camera augmentation during layout comparisons and adds a separate camera-augmentation on/off control. Appendix F.4 specifies a 50K-image grounding protocol for the added synthetic-baseline comparison. The original Tasks 1–5 retain their splits, metrics, and training schedules; newly disclosed budgets for older comparisons do not establish that those budgets changed.

E4.justification: v2 tests 3D versus alternative layouts, separately measures camera augmentation, and revises the harmonization ablation. It removes the quantitative Subject200K segment-quality comparison and v1's reported ControlNet/inpainting training-failure analysis. The appendix scaling ablations, FID analysis, and human segment-quality assessment remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports downstream repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The use of different generation seeds for synthetic segments is retained and does not constitute new experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds SegGen results of 9.73 COCO AP and 36.8 LVIS-Mini AP, and SynGround gRefCOCO results of 40.1 P@1 and 89.2 no-target accuracy. Revised ablations report 10.03 AP for 3D layout and 6.28 without harmonization, while removing the Subject200K 12.06 entry. These concern revised configurations, not established same-setting gains. Main benchmark tables and Figures 4–7 retain their numerical results.

T1.justification: Sections 3.2 and 3.4 introduce a formal category-independence assumption, stochastic 3D scene construction, perspective-projection equations, and a depth-dependent blur definition. These mathematical specifications were absent from v1's 2D layout procedure. The appendix blending equations remain equivalent; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: v2 makes 3D layout and camera augmentation central contributions and adds explicit claims of being the first large synthetic dataset to surpass real datasets across diverse models and tasks, and of outperforming all existing synthetic pipelines. These broaden v1's claims about scalable composition and benefits against selected real-data and copy-paste baselines.

C2.justification: v2 adds the explanation that category-independent geometry and camera perturbations suppress pictorial shortcuts and encourage view-invariant representations. It also attributes the largest ablation gain to generative harmonization. Existing long-tail, scaling, and FID interpretations and Appendix A limitations are retained, including the unreconciled statement that the pipeline lacks explicit 3D constraints.

D1.justification: New Appendix F.4 documents synthetic-comparison budgets of 10K images for COCO and 50K for detection/grounding, together with initialization, hardware, batch size, and learning rate. v2 also specifies augmentation parameters such as zoom factors, aperture range, and the overlap rejection threshold. Existing prompt templates and original task-training recipes are retained; these disclosures do not prove older experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v2 adds a focused image-matting and harmonization discussion with six matting references, plus MonoPair and the FID reference. It foregrounds comparisons with mask-conditioned diffusion methods and strengthens novelty positioning. Most cited literature and the detailed appendix related-work discussion are retained.

P1.justification: Beyond the SOS-to-SOC and title changes, v2 substantially reorganizes the Method section, rewrites the main related-work discussion, condenses annotation and dataset explanations, and adds an explicit contribution list. It also removes the gallery sections I–K. These constitute substantial narrative and structural editing.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves to the first page and gains a schematic performance panel. Figure 2 is redrawn around 3D geometry and camera augmentation. v2 adds a capability-comparison table, restructures the synthetic-baseline and ablation tables, and resizes or relocates retained displays. The extensive training-image and object-segment galleries, including duplicated examples, are removed.

improvement.justification: The added baseline results, component controls, and explicit comparison budgets improve empirical coverage and reproducibility. However, v2 introduces claims that conflict with its evidence: the introduction claims a COCO gain over SynGround, while Table 5 reports only grounding results for it. The new 3D procedure is also unreconciled with Appendix A, and the Subject200K superiority claim remains after its quantitative result is removed. These competing changes prevent a reliable judgment of net overall quality.
